# diff-audit — source and diff ledger

Coverage unit: one ordinary unified Git hunk from `git diff -- src/data`. **377 items**. CORRECT 144; WRONG 17; UNPROVEN 216.
Hunks with a matching table row: **363**. Hunks without a matching table row: **14**. The unlogged mirror edits are described narratively in B lines22-24; under the requested row-based rule they still have no matching row.

**DO NOT COMMIT.** Nine positive-supply pins were changed to ground. Additional board-layout, shared-builder and printed-page regressions are established below.

## Limits of this ledger

Every hunk is inventoried below with a decision and the complete changed lines. This is not a claim that every changed hardware assertion was proven. UNPROVEN explicitly includes source readings not completed; those items are not approved. CORRECT for a pure flag/removal means that the requested warning/removal is honest; it does not certify the unchanged underlying claim. A WRONG decision establishes at least the contradiction stated, not every other claim in the same hunk.

636 distinct citation URLs from affected runtime records were attempted with curl -L -A Mozilla/5.0, stored under diff-audit/. Windows curl HTTPS failed with SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS; urllib was used as a TLS fallback. Each URL has sNNN.fetch.json with status/error, plus source bytes when retrieved.173 PDFs were detected in these requests and processed by pdftotext -layout. Archive details URLs are landing pages, not evidence;57 archive item metadata records were also requested and available book PDFs downloaded and extracted. Some collections contained multiple books, so downloading one collection PDF is explicitly not proof of all its citations. Scanned pages actually used for findings were rendered with pdftoppm -f N -l N -r110 -png and inspected.

Archive numbering: viewer /page/n239 is zero-based leaf239, hence PDF page240. Printed page labels are read from the actual rendered page, not inferred by adding an offset.

## Established findings

### High: positive supply changed to ground — boundary-discipline

| Chip | Pin | Correct identity | Source independently read | Hunk |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| cpu7501 | 5 | VCC,+5 V | TED Hardware Manual14 | H145 |
| cpu6502 | 8 | VCC,+5 V | MOS6500Nov1985 p10 | H091 |
| cpu6502c | 8 | VCC,+5 V | 600XL FSM1-5,Fig1-3/PDF15 | H108 |
| cpuz80 | 11 | +5 V | UM0080 p5/PDF19,Fig3 | H303 |
| cpu8088 | 40 | VCC,+5 V | Intel1983 p3-79/PDF259,Fig2 | H257 |
| cpu6809e | 7 | VCC,+5 V | MotorolaMC6809E p1 | H330 |
| pal40030 | 20 | VCC,+5 V | CPC6128schematic19-20/PDF17,IC118 | H052 |
| cpu65sc12 | 8 | VDD,+5 V | Master0143,000 sheet1,IC14/supplytable | H019 |
| cpu6808 | 8 | VCC,+5 V | MotorolaDS9818-R3 p1 | H232 |

All nine are logged in A/B Additional corrections, so this is not an unlogged-change allegation. Several retain vcc glossary tags and+5 V probe expectations. A ground clip placed on any such supply can short the board rail. Shared records multiply the affected machines.

### High: BBC analogue fix leaks to the Master — boundary-discipline

Shared anaPins changes PB5/PB4 references to IC3 for BOTH BBC B and Master. Master drawing0143,000 sheet2 identifies the system VIA as IC8; IC3 is WD1770. Correct Master text is IC8 pin15/PB5 and IC8 pin14/PB4, or omit board designators from this shared builder.
Runtime proof: diff-audit/runtime-boundary-proof.json; rendered master-sheet2.png.

### High: Electron package repair leaves wrong numbering — redesign-from-first-principles

Electron SM p.8/PDF14 places pin1 at top left and consecutive numbering anticlockwise. pkg PLCC-68 still calls actual plccPlace(0,17) -> top slot8 (mid-top), and puts pin9 at top-left. The new wording does not repair the wrong physical pin layout. Correct the package/renderer mapping to the manual before accepting this fix.
The actual renderer function was executed, not just its comments read. Runtime proof records pin1 top slot8 and pin9 top slot0. Source: Electron SM printed8/PDF14, electron-ula-manual.png.

### Medium: Disk II printed-page corrections regress — foundational-thinking

Five changed hunks (six labels) move correct printed page numbers one forward. Figure9.7 is9-10; Table9.1 is9-11; Drive Off/On is9-13. Proof images: sather-fig97.png, sather-table91.png, sather-driveoffon.png. H074,H075,H077,H079,H083.

### Medium: TS1000 new verification flags are invisible — boundary-discipline

New verify:true flags on TS1000 Power in and GND rails are invisible: actual viewPower rail template reads neither r.verify nor r.conflict. The source log says these claims needed verification; data still presents them without CHECK. Remove unproved details or use an uncertainty field that the current rail view displays.
Runtime proof: runtime-boundary-proof.json; source code renderer src/app.js Rails block.

### Medium: exact HERO duty is unproven — foundational-thinking

H249/H252 justify50% from equal minimum widths. A minimum is a bound, not a measured or guaranteed duty. These remain UNPROVEN; remove the exact duty unless another source proves it.

## Source removal / weakening audit

Compared before/after runtime citation sets, preserving source identity across inserted array elements. No source list or whole document was removed from a surviving record. Master analogue swaps the same manual anchor40 for41; PDF41 is printed40, making the destination more accurate while the label continues to say printed40. Mirror insertion shifts array indices but does not delete the displaced source. Shared-chip edits were examined in the semantic diff; board-labelled C64/HERO Jr details remain explicitly scoped. The unqualified Master IC3 leakage and nine shared supply corruptions are the established shared-data failures.

### H001 — src/data/acorn.js:93 — WRONG

Shared anaPins changes PB5/PB4 references to IC3 for BOTH BBC B and Master. Master drawing0143,000 sheet2 identifies the system VIA as IC8; IC3 is WD1770. Correct Master text is IC8 pin15/PB5 and IC8 pin14/PB4, or omit board designators from this shared builder.

Fix-log mapping:
- fixes-b.md line101:  /  07:218  /  UNVER  /  acorn.js master-analogue pin 11  /  desc: Converter reference, from three diodes (about 1.8 V). Use it as the top of the paddle pots.  /  desc: Converter reference, from three diodes (about 1.8 V): the full-scale input.  /  Master manual 26,41,52  / 
- fixes-b.md line103:  /  07:220  /  UNVER  /  acorn.js master-analogue pin 13  /  name: PB0 (fire 0); desc: Digital input I0, a fire button to the system VIA port B.; verify: -  /  name: PB4 (fire 0); desc: Digital input I0, a fire button to system VIA PB4 (IC3 pin 14).; verify: true  /  Master manual 26,41,52  / 
- fixes-b.md line917:  /  35:200  /  WRONG  /  acorn.js bbcb-analogue pin 10  /  name: PB1 (fire 1); desc: Digital input I1, a fire button to the system VIA port B.  /  name: PB5 (fire 1); desc: Digital input I1, a fire button to system VIA PB5 (IC3 pin 15).  /  Acorn103,000/C issue9 sheet1 bbcb-analogue; S28pp41,52/S32ch26  / 
- fixes-b.md line162:  /  08:15  /  UNVER  /  acorn.js bbcb rail +5 V  /  expect: 4.9-5.2 V; note: Fed at three points and joined on the board (Model B issue 2 linear boards have been found with the points not joined).  /  expect: +5 V; note: Fed at three points and joined on the board (RetroTechWiki: Model B issue 2 linear boards have been found with the points not joined).  /  B §§3.14,6.3; S sheet 1; B85 p.24  / 

Affected runtime records: connectors.bbcmaster.5, connectors.bbcb.5, connectors.bbcmaster.3, connectors.bbcb.3, BAT3_PADS, BAT3_OUTLINE, rgbPins
